claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in HEAs is governed primarily by the formation and stability of a nanocrystalline, compositionally complex passive oxide layer.
The passive oxide layer acts as a barrier to both mechanical abrasion and electrochemical attack.
The effectiveness of the passive layer depends on synergistic effects among multiple principal elements.
Synergistic effects among multiple principal elements enhance passivation kinetics.
Synergistic effects among multiple principal elements reduce localized passive-film breakdown.
A nanocrystalline, multi-element passive oxide layer forms in situ during simultaneous wear and corrosion exposure.
The multi-element oxide layer forms rapidly because of high configurational entropy and mutual solubility of the alloying elements.
The nanocrystalline structure and compositional complexity of the oxide increase its mechanical hardness.
The nanocrystalline structure and compositional complexity of the oxide reduce its defect density.
Greater oxide hardness and lower defect density increase resistance to wear-induced film removal.
Greater oxide hardness and lower defect density increase resistance to corrosion-induced dissolution.
Synergistic effects among alloying elements suppress localized corrosion such as pitting.
Maintenance of a continuous protective film reduces wear rates.
The HEA will have a significantly lower combined degradation rate than a conventional stainless-steel or single-principal-element baseline under identical conditions.
The HEA's wear loss will be at least 30–50% lower than that of the baseline.
The HEA's corrosion current will be at least 30–50% lower than that of the baseline.
The HEA passive layer will remain intact longer than the baseline's protective layer.
Pitting and spalling events will be less frequent in the HEA than in the baseline.
The prediction should hold for HEAs containing sufficient passivating elements such as Cr, Al, or Mo under moderate mechanical and electrochemical stress.
The prediction may fail for HEAs lacking passivating elements or under loads or potentials that exceed passive-layer stability.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies an acidic chloride environment, but the stated conditions and experimental design specify only 0.5 M NaCl without an acid concentration or pH; unmodified NaCl does not by itself define an acidic environment.
